extraction.name: LAMBADA
extraction.description: LAMBADA is a dataset to evaluate the capabilities of computational models for text understanding by means of a word prediction task. It is a collection of narrative passages sharing the characteristic that human subjects are able to guess their last word if they are exposed to the whole passage, but not if they only see the last sentence preceding the target word.
extraction.creator: Denis Paperno, Germán Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bernardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Fernández
extraction.citeAs: Denis Paperno, Germán Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bernardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Fernández. 2016. The LAMBADA dataset: Word prediction requiring a broad discourse context. In Proceedings of the 54th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, pages 1525–1534, Berlin, Germany.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The LAMBADA data come from the Book Corpus. The corpus, after duplicate removal and filtering out of potentially offensive material with a stop word list, contains 5,325 novels and 465 million words. Novels were randomly divided into equally-sized training and development+testing partitions. Passages were filtered using a combination of four language models to exclude passages that are relatively easy for standard language models. Any passage whose target word had probability ≥0.00175 according to any of the language models was excluded.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Book Corpus containing unpublished novels. The corpus contains 5,325 novels and 465 million words after duplicate removal and filtering.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Passages were filtered using a combination of four language models (a pre-trained recurrent neural network, a standard 4-gram model, a RNN and a feed-forward model trained on the Book Corpus). Any passage whose target word had probability ≥0.00175 according to any of the language models was excluded. Novels were randomly divided into equally-sized training and development+testing partitions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The corpus underwent duplicate removal and filtering out of potentially offensive material with a stop word list. Passages were constructed with a context (on average 4.6 sentences) and a target sentence, where the context size is the minimum number of complete sentences before the target sentence such that they cumulatively contain at least 50 tokens. The target word is constrained to be the last word of the sentence.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human subjects evaluated passages through the CrowdFlower crowdsourcing service in three steps: (1) one human subject guessed the target word based on the whole passage; if correct, (2) a second subject guessed the target word based on the whole passage; if also correct, (3) more subjects tried to guess the target word based on the target sentence only, until the word was guessed or the number of unsuccessful guesses reached 10. If no subject was able to guess the target word from the sentence alone, the passage was added to LAMBADA. Subjects in step 3 were allowed 3 guesses per sentence. The same subject could not judge the same item in both passage and sentence conditions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The criteria for passage inclusion were very strict: two consecutive subjects were required to exactly match the missing word, and no subject (out of ten) was able to provide it based on local context only, even when given 3 guesses. In the crowdsourcing pipeline, 84–86% items were discarded at step 1, an additional 6–7% at step 2 and another 3–5% at step 3. Only about one in 25 input examples passed all the selection steps.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Multiple annotations per item: 2 subjects for broad context validation (steps 1 and 2), and up to 10 subjects for sentence-only context testing (step 3)
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Four language models were used for initial filtering: a pre-trained recurrent neural network (RNN), a standard 4-gram model, a RNN, and a feed-forward model trained on the Book Corpus
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The development set of LAMBADA, along with the training corpus, can be downloaded at http://clic.cimec.unitn.it/lambada/. The test set will be made available at the time of the competition.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: More than 80% of LAMBADA passages include the target word in the context. Most target words in LAMBADA are proper nouns (48%), followed by common nouns (37%) and verbs (7.7%). Proper nouns are hugely over-represented in LAMBADA compared to the input data POS distribution. The LAMBADA items contain (quoted) direct speech significantly more often than the input items overall (71% of LAMBADA items vs. 61% of items in the input sample).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to passages where the target word can be exactly matched by human subjects (perfect-match approach). Alternative plausible or synonymous continuations were not considered due to practical and methodological challenges. The constraint that the target word be the last word of the sentence, while not necessary for the research goal, makes the task more natural for human subjects. The dataset focuses on narrative passages from unpublished novels, which may limit generalization to other text genres.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is meant to evaluate the capabilities of computational models for text understanding by means of a word prediction task. It is designed as a challenging test set to encourage the development of new models capable of genuine understanding of broad context in natural language text. Models should be trained on the LAMBADA training data (203 million words from 2,662 novels) using standard language modeling approaches. The development data can be used to fine-tune models to the specifics of the LAMBADA passages.
